sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Schiedam, next to Rotterdam, has extended paid parking from its historic centre outwards and is cautious about extending it further. The parking tax ordinance, in force in its 2026 form from 1 January, charges 3.32 euros an hour in sector A, the historic centre, with a maximum of 19.92 euros, and 2.39 euros an hour in sectors B to F, with a maximum of 13.15 euros [0]. A first resident permit costs 90.10 euros a year, a second 224.70 euros and a third 360.45 euros [1]. Visitor parking costs 0.46 euro an hour for residents, up to 400 hours a year, and the additional assessment is 82.00 euros with no remission [2]. The executive replaced the annex on where and when paid parking applies, with effect from 1 May 2026: Monday to Friday from 09.00 to 20.00 and Saturday until 17.00 in sectors A, C and E, and Monday to Saturday until 23.00 in sectors B (Schiedam-Oost) and F (Nieuw-Mathenesse) [3]. The municipality announced on 27 January 2026 that it had reconsidered a plan of 14 January to extend paid parking to 23.00 everywhere, so that drivers from Rotterdam-West, where paid parking already runs to 23.00, do not move into Schiedam-Oost and Nieuw-Mathenesse; the other sectors keep their hours for the time being [5]. The permit rules allow at most one resident permit per address in sectors A and E and two in B, C and D, with second permits in sector B capped at 250 addresses [10]. Regulated parking can come to a new neighbourhood only after a support survey that needs requests from at least 10 percent of adult residents, and an interim count of April 2026 showed requests in 14 neighbourhoods, the highest being 0.90 percent in the Fabribuurt, far below the threshold [7][8].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Nieuw-Mathenesse is the new frontier. Paid parking has applied there since 1 May 2026, at 2.39 euros an hour, to support a car-light Glasbuurt with about 1,300 new homes whose future residents are to park in two future garages and pay for a space there to make the garages financially feasible; there was no support survey because the area is a business park without residents [6]. The mobility norms of July 2024 give most functions in the inner city a parking norm of zero, because plots are built up or pedestrianised and garages exist [11]. On charging, the municipality has joined Rotterdam's charging strategy for 2026 to 2035, under which residents and businesses can no longer apply for public charge points from 1 January 2026 and the municipality places them based on forecasts, with TotalEnergies and Velian to install them from 2027 [17]. The tariff at the municipal SGZH 2.0 posts stays at 0.37 euro per kWh for the rest of 2026 [18].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality lists three garages in the centre, ABC, Passage and Stadserf, with the first hour free in ABC and Passage, and two park-and-rides, P+R Schiedam Centrum with more than 750 spaces on Noorderweg, for which it refers readers to the operator's page for tariffs, and P+R Horvathweg with 64 spaces; it also lists the free car park at Vijfsluizen metro station [12]. Interparking operates the ABC garage, with 325 spaces, where the first hour is free and then it costs 0.50 euro per 20 minutes with a maximum of 15 euros a day [14]. The Passage garage has 280 spaces and the same tariff [13]. Q-Park's page shows 64 spaces at Horvathweg, with its tariffs not loading [16]. Visitors of residents park through the digital BezoekersApp at 0.46 euro an hour, and from 1 May 2026 businesses can use it at 1.14 euros an hour [19].

Our data cover the P+R at Vijfsluizen, with 88 spaces, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 41% on weekdays and 26% at weekends, and it reached full in a single reading on a Monday morning, which fits a commuter car park next to the metro. The garages in the centre are not in our data.
